name: sgs/before-after
title: Before / After
description: Two-media comparison slider with a draggable divider. Each side (before/after) independently chooses image / video / SVG via `beforeMediaType`/`afterMediaType` — mirroring sgs/media's mediaType fork applied per comparison slot. Works with zero JavaScript for the image/SVG case — both slots are always present in the markup and a CSS-only clip-path renders the configured default position; JS progressively enhances the divider into a live drag (native range input for keyboard + touch, GSAP Draggable for free-drag directly on the media) and, when either slot is video, drives synchronised play/pause + drift-corrected currentTime across both `<video>` elements. Video slots support WP-library uploads and direct MP4/WebM URLs ONLY — YouTube/Vimeo embeds are deliberately unsupported here because a cross-origin iframe cannot be kept in sync without loading each platform's external player SDK (Spec 38 three-tier motion doctrine: no CDN-loaded third-party script). `orientation` (horizontal/vertical) crossed with `reverseDirection` gives all four reveal directions — after-on-left (default), after-on-right, after-on-top, after-on-bottom — with the label order and clip-path both keyed off the same two attributes so a label never sits over the wrong media. Content-KIND, block-private (no SGS_Container_Wrapper) — box + width only, matches the sgs/quote / sgs/button pattern (D294).

sgs._comment_mediaElements: Wave 5b. Replaces the old universal imageControls extension's single shared sgsObjectFit/sgsObjectPosition pair (which set BOTH the before and after slots identically) with two independently-scoped media elements, one per slot.

label.label: Labels
label._note: 'fill' cluster added 2026-08-15 so labelBackgroundColour (previously an unclaimed style-defect orphan) resolves via the default convention: label + BackgroundColour. labelColour already resolved fine under 'text' (css:color, suffix Colour). Gradient siblings for both added 2026-09-04 as explicit attrMap entries (the default convention's suffix table doesn't cover *ColourGradient/*BackgroundColourGradient) — labelBackgroundColourGradient moved to its own ::after layer (sgs_block_background_layer_css()) to free the element's background-image for labelColourGradient's background-clip:text.
label._note_bg: labelBackgroundColour declared 2026-09-05: read at render.php:141 and painted as the label's own background. render.php:283 records it was deliberately moved OFF the shared mechanism, which is why nothing declared it and it showed as a rogue seed.

divider-line.label: Divider line
divider-line._note: The visible divider stroke rendered inside the divider assembly (`.wp-block-sgs-before-after__divider-line`, render.php line 558) — a child of the `divider` element's positioning wrapper, NOT the same node. dividerColour/dividerWidth were previously misattributed as orphans under `divider` by simple prefix-string matching (both names literally start with 'divider'); this explicit attrMap claims them on their real owning element instead, clearing both from the conformance style-defect count. css:width is used for the line's thickness (DB records the underlying CSS as a height+width shorthand); no dedicated stroke-thickness member exists in the taxonomy, so css:width/layout is the nearest honest mapping. Found live 2026-08-15: DB tagged 2 attrs css_element='divider-line', undeclared until now.

handle.label: Handle
handle._note: The draggable divider handle/grip (`.wp-block-sgs-before-after__handle`, render.php line 559). handleColour paints its background. handleIconColour styles the icon's SVG stroke — a property with no cluster-member analogue anywhere in cluster-member-sets.json (no css:stroke member exists in the current taxonomy), so it is deliberately left unclustered rather than force-fit into background-color. `prefix: ""` opts this element out of orphan-candidate scanning so handleIconColour is reported honestly as an accepted gap (adding a css:stroke member is a framework-level taxonomy change, out of scope for a single block's manifest). Found live 2026-08-15: DB tagged 2 attrs css_element='handle', undeclared until now. 2026-09-05 (svg-paint-gradient end-shape): handleIconColourGradient added as the FIRST svg-paint-gradient row in the framework — resolved via sgs_svg_stroke_gradient() (same mechanism as sgs/icon's iconColourGradient), never the background-image custom-property-gradient pattern used elsewhere on this same block, because a stroke gradient needs a real SVG <linearGradient>/<radialGradient> def, not a CSS background paint. css:stroke/css:stroke-gradient entries added here rather than to cluster-member-sets.json (still no framework-wide stroke-gradient vocabulary member — same scope boundary as the note above).

attributes._comment_ssr_nullable: Every numeric attribute below whose default is null is declared as [ <numeric>, "string" ] — the house convention (sgs/heading, sgs/text). REASON: this block previews through <ServerSideRender>, which serialises an unset attribute as an EMPTY STRING into the block-renderer REST query. A schema of plain "integer"/"number" rejects "", the REST call returns HTTP 400, and the editor shows 'Preview failed to load' for every instance — while the frontend renders perfectly, so no frontend check can catch it. Found live 2026-07-31 by the Wave C editor probe (D388). render.php already coerces with (int) / a null check, so accepting "" changes no rendered output.

beforeMediaType._comment: Mirrors sgs/media's mediaType fork (Spec 38 Step 6), applied per comparison slot rather than block-wide — the before side and after side may each be a different media type (e.g. an SVG diagram compared against a photo).

beforeImageDecorative.description: When true, this slot's image renders with an empty alt and aria-hidden so screen readers skip it, per D918/S8 naming convention ({element}Decorative).

afterImageDecorative.description: When true, this slot's image renders with an empty alt and aria-hidden so screen readers skip it, per D918/S8 naming convention ({element}Decorative).

attributes._comment_artDirection: Art-direction tiers (2026-08-07) — the IMAGE pair, completing the half this block was missing: its VIDEO playback tiers landed at d8cdcf8b. Same {base}/{base}Tablet/{base}Mobile shape and ID-wins-URL-falls-back pairing as sgs/media and sgs/hero. Alt text is deliberately NOT tiered — a different crop of the same subject describes the same thing, and a per-device alt would be a second place for the description to drift out of sync. Tier siblings render inside their own comparison slot so the divider still clips them.

videoAutoplay._comment: Gated behind prefers-reduced-motion at render time in view.js — reduced motion always starts both videos paused regardless of this attribute; the shared play/pause toggle remains available either way (explicit user action, never suppressed).

videoAutoplayTablet._comment: Per-device playback tier (D-pending). null = inherit the tier above (Tablet inherits Desktop, Mobile inherits Tablet) — same convention as sgs/media's videoAutoplayTablet/Mobile and every other *Tablet/*Mobile attr in this framework. Still gated behind prefers-reduced-motion at whichever tier is effective. 'string' is in the type union ONLY because @wordpress/server-side-render's GET transport serialises a null attribute value to an empty string in the REST query string (addQueryArgs cannot represent a real null) — without 'string' here, block-renderer's own schema validation 400s the editor's own live preview on every load (confirmed live 2026-09-01: rest_invalid_param, '[videoAutoplayTablet] is not of type boolean,null.'). render.php treats an empty string identically to null (inherit) — see the raw-value guard below.

reverseDirection._comment: Crossed with orientation to give all 4 reveal directions. false (default, UNCHANGED — Bean-locked): horizontal reveals after on the LEFT, vertical reveals after on the TOP. true: horizontal reveals after on the RIGHT (the more common slider convention), vertical reveals after on the BOTTOM. style.css keys both the clip-path AND the label order off this same attribute so a direction change can never reintroduce the 2026-07-31 label-vs-image mismatch (labels + clip must always move together).

fxDraggable._comment: Spec 38 FR-38-13 roster opt-in. When true, GSAP Draggable enhances the divider so the visitor can drag anywhere on the image, on top of the always-present native range input (keyboard + native touch drag + no-JS-safe). When false, only the native range input drives the divider — still fully operable, just without the free-drag-on-image layer.

dividerColourGradient.description: CSS gradient string painting via background-image (helpers-tokens.php sgs_custom_property_gradient_decls). Non-empty wins over dividerColour.

handleIconColourGradient.description: CSS gradient string painting the handle icon's SVG stroke via a real <linearGradient>/<radialGradient> def (sgs_svg_stroke_gradient(), same mechanism as sgs/icon's iconColourGradient) rather than the background-image custom-property pattern used elsewhere on this block (D636 gradient rollout, extended 2026-09-05 — the ONLY svg-paint-gradient row in the framework at the time this was added). Non-empty wins over handleIconColour at paint time.

handleIconSource.description: IconPicker source for the draggable handle's icon glyph (2026-09-05 migration off the hand-rolled two-polyline SVG onto the shared Lucide+IconPicker mechanism, matching sgs/icon's iconSource/iconName pair). Restricted to the two inline-SVG sources (lucide/wp-icon) — dashicon (font glyph) and emoji (text glyph) have no SVG stroke for a gradient to paint, unlike sgs/icon which supports all four sources for its FLAT colour. Defaults to 'lucide' + handleIconName='chevrons-left-right' so every existing instance renders visually unchanged.

handleIconName.description: Lucide/wp-icon/dashicon slug for the handle icon. Default 'chevrons-left-right' matches the previously hand-rolled two-polyline chevron SVG exactly — no visual regression on un-migrated instances.

borderColourGradient.description: CSS gradient string painting the border with a masked ring instead of a flat colour (D636 border-gradient rollout). Non-empty wins over borderColour.
